definitions.explanation: Describes something that causes fear or is frightening. Can also describe the feeling of being scared.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{怖|こわ}かった⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
⟦{暗|くら}い→暗い：00647_kurai⟧⟦ところ→ところ：01137_tokoro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{怖|こわ}い⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
{怖|こわ}い⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}ました→見る：00283_miru⟧。
⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{怖|こわ}くて、⟦{近|ちか}づけません→近づく：01958_chikazuku⟧。
examples.english: I'm scared of dogs, so I can't go near them.
When I was a child, I was scared of going outside alone at night.

notes:
{怖|こわ}い is an i-adjective meaning 'scary' or 'frightening.' Unlike English, Japanese uses the same word for both 'scary' (describing the stimulus) and 'scared' (describing the feeling)—context determines the meaning.

GRAMMAR:
- {怖|こわ}くて ({連用形|れんようけい}): 'scary and...' or 'because it's scary'
- {怖|こわ}くない: 'not scary'
- {怖|こわ}かった: 'was scary'
- {怖|こわ}がる: verb form meaning 'to be afraid of' or 'to act scared'

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {怖|こわ}い{話|はなし}: scary story, ghost story
- {怖|こわ}い{夢|ゆめ}: nightmare, scary dream
- {怖|こわ}くて{仕方|しかた}がない: to be terrified, can't help being scared
- {怖|こわ}いもの{知|し}らず: fearless (literally 'not knowing scary things')

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {恐|おそ}ろしい: terrifying (stronger, more literary)
- {気味|きみ}が{悪|わる}い: creepy, eerie
- ビビる: to be freaked out (slang)
